messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High KV cache memory growth observed on us-east-1-gpu-pool-3. 90th/99th token latency spikes and OOM traces starting 3891234567. Autoscaler reporting rate-limit fallbacks for several hostgroups. See summary below.

marta: seeing same — p50 ok but tail is awful, many requests stuck in cont-batching for >200ms. Dashboard: cache_used ~ 92% vs normal 48%. :frowning_face:

cory: any obvious change rolled out? recent model or batching config?

marta: we rolled a batch window tweak two days ago on the canary but it hit prod via a global rollout 6h ago — suspected culprit: `batch_window_ms` bumped from 8->20 to improve throughput.

jamie: I can take page. Oncall here. What's impact to customers?

emily: some enterprise customers seeing degraded generation latency, two support tickets (SUP-10290, SUP-10291). No full service outage but SLA breaches for priority routes.

marta: syslogs show repeated `cudaMalloc` failures + high fragmentation in the KV arena. Snippet from node logs:```
[E] kv_cache.cpp:237 alloc_key_slot failed: arena_alloc returned null
[E] cuda_mem.cc:112 cudaMalloc 0x0 -> OUT_OF_MEMORY (attempt=3)
WARN continuous_batcher.cpp:334 flush delayed due to kv_lock contention
```

cory: that lines up with fragmentation — the arena is refusing to satisfy small slab allocs and the cont-batcher is accumulating requests until they overflow.

jamie: mitigation plan options: 1) rollback batch_window to 8ms (fast revert), 2) apply per-host temporary throttle to `max_batch_size` to reduce allocation concurrency, 3) force arena compaction on hosts, 4) enable fallback to smaller model variants if allocation fails. Suggest do 1+2 immediately.

marta: prepared a hotfix PR for the controller config to set `global.batch_window_ms=8` and `route_override.max_batch_size=64` for affected routes. PR link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/6421 — waiting to deploy if oncall wants.

jamie: please deploy hotfix to a small subset first (10% traffic) then ramp. I will run the following commands to push the config to the fleet:```bash
# push config to controller
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"batch_window_ms":8, "max_batch_size":64}' https://controller.redwood.internal/v1/overrides/apply
# mark a canary group
rlctl rollout --group canary-gpu-3 --config controller-overrides.json
```

deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollout id r-2026-3891, group canary-gpu-3, user=jamie

jamie: executing now. I'll also add a temporary throttle rule to the router to cap concurrent in-flight requests per host to 200.

marta: started running `nvprof`/memstats capture on a few hosts and will gather `pytorch` allocator dumps. Will also run our `arena-compactor` utility with `--aggressive` if rollback doesn't help.

cory: note — compaction is relatively heavy, will cause brief additional CPU pressure. Use during low-traffic window or stagger across hosts.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout r-2026-3891 successful on group canary-gpu-3 (10% traffic).

jamie: canary metrics look promising: cache_used down from 92%->71% on canary hosts, tail latency improving ~35%. Holding for 5m then ramp.

emily: I've informed support and updated incident channel with SUP numbers. Customer-facing note drafted: "We're seeing elevated latencies due to internal batching config regression; a mitigation rollout is in progress."

jamie: ramping to 50% now. If no regression in 10m, full ramp.

deploy-bot: Rollout r-2026-3891 to 50% complete.

marta: after ramp to 50% we saw mixed results — overall memory usage dropped but some hosts still show fragmentation and occasional `cudaMalloc` OOMs. Attached allocator dump shows many small live slabs: `slab_utilization: small(4k)=86%, medium(64k)=72%, large(1M)=13%` — lots of small churn.

cory: that suggests KV slab mixing causing internal fragmentation. Two additional actions: - enable temporary aggressive KV eviction policy (`evict_age_ms=3000`) to reduce live footprint - roll out a background arena compaction with `--visit-window=30s` staggered 30s apart.

jamie: apply eviction policy across fleet via controller, low-risk. Marta, can you coordinate compaction windows?

marta: scheduling compaction across hosts now, 30s stagger, on a rolling basis to avoid simultaneous CPU hit. Command:```bash
ssh host-$i 'arena-compactor --aggressive --visit-window=30s' &
```

dave: question — should we also tweak `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` to use `max_split_size_mb` to reduce fragmentation? We can set `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64` via env for the runtime and restart process — but that's more invasive.

cory: agreed it's higher risk. Consider for next maintenance window. For now compaction + throttles + eviction should relieve pressure.

jamie: after compaction started I'm seeing `cudaMalloc` errors drop on compaction hosts. Canary hosts back to normal; ramping to 100%.

deploy-bot: Rollout r-2026-3891 completed to 100% traffic. change_id=6421

emily: support update: SUP-10290 resolved (customer saw latency return to normal), SUP-10291 still investigating but improving.

marta: post-mortem notes so far: root cause: change to `batch_window_ms` increased concurrent KV allocations and cont-batch accumulation causing arena fragmentation and `cudaMalloc` pressure. Secondary factors: small-slab churn pattern in KV allocator and lack of aggressive eviction during sustained load.

cory: immediate follow-ups: 1) revert batch_window_ms to 8ms (done) 2) add a safety circuit to prevent >x% global rollout for batch config changes without perf test 3) implement automatic arena compaction heuristic when fragmentation > 70% 4) evaluate `max_split_size_mb` patch in staging.

jamie: leaving oncall to cory for next 8h. I'll create the incident runbook entry and schedule RCA meeting.

jamie: handoff: oncall -> cory. TL;DR: hotpatch rollback deployed, eviction + compaction performed, customer impact limited, monitoring to confirm stability.

cory: taking over. Thanks team. I'll keep nightly watch and open ticket INC-3891 for long-term allocator work.

emily: adding incident summary to statuspage draft. Will ping when public note ready. :white_check_mark:

marta: saved logs and allocator dumps to: s3://redwood-incidents/3891234567/ for RCA.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-3891 created, severity: Sev2, assigned: cory, pager oncall: cory

jamie: thanks all — nice rapid triage. Next steps tracked in INC-3891.

marta: postscript: recommend we add a canary perf test targeting batching + KV under realistic small-slab churn by next sprint to catch this earlier.

cory: noted.
